traffic: TelcoMind traffic burst experiments increase downlink UDP offered traffic during a bounded middle window while keeping stationary UEs and resource bands unchanged. Compare measured throughput and mean delay before, during, and after the burst. Phase throughput uses each observation window, including drain time in the final window. Increased offered traffic is not proof of congestion: establish whether delivery or delay deteriorated using measured results and explicit targets. This experiment does not inject radio interference.
resources: TelcoMind resource comparison experiments execute two fresh stationary downlink runs with identical UE count, seed, duration, packet size, and send interval. Only the configured number of resource bands differs. Compare candidate minus reference throughput, mean delay, and undelivered percentage points. Equal performance can mean the tested load did not expose a resource constraint; do not invent an improvement. Resource band changes are not network slicing or an automated remediation.
mobility: TelcoMind mobility handover experiments use linear UE movement, dynamic cell association, enabled NR handovers, and X2 links between all seven base stations. Serving-cell vectors record simulator node IDs. Exclude initial association and count subsequent ID changes as serving-cell transitions; report transitions to node ID zero separately as detachments. A transition count is not a handover attempt denominator or a standardized success rate. Correlate transition times with measured downlink throughput and delay, but do not infer a handover failure solely from an undelivered packet. No controlled handover fault is injected.
